raw_response: {"sentences":[{"text":"Leaving Pont Neuf behind, head for Square du Vert-Galant, just ahead.","source_id":"GLUE_NAV","source_type":"glue","stop_idx":1},{"text":"Take the steps down behind Henri IV's equestrian statue on the Pont-Neuf and you drop into the triangular stern of the island, the Square du Vert-Galant.","source_id":"53261606-2bd8-4862-829f-6730c31f2b4d","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":1,"also_cites":["391c501b-9c3d-49e0-91fb-ebe55a456262"]},{"text":"This romantic western tip of the boat-shaped Île de la Cité is where Paris began — the original settlement of the Parisii, a Celtic tribe subdued by Caesar, on the island the Romans called Lutetia.","source_id":"7e2bf42c-6255-4fd7-9d74-7866cde485f3","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":1},{"text":"The late Roman emperor Julian, writing in 358 AD, called it Cara Lutetia — \"my beloved Lutetia.\"","source_id":"7e2bf42c-6255-4fd7-9d74-7866cde485f3","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":1},{"text":"As for the name Vert-Galant, it means the Green Gallant, the lusty gentleman — a nod to the king's famously amorous career.","source_id":"391c501b-9c3d-49e0-91fb-ebe55a456262","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":1,"also_cites":["53261606-2bd8-4862-829f-6730c31f2b4d"]},{"text":"Henri loved this city mightily, and loved its wine, women, and good times just as hard: two wives, at least fifty-six mistresses, and households full of bastards.","source_id":"7e2bf42c-6255-4fd7-9d74-7866cde485f3","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":1},{"text":"Early on, Parisians adored him for it — but the charm faded as he aged, and his serial affairs began to bore and irritate.","source_id":"af6c2d1f-72f5-4778-94a1-466874d65049","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":1,"also_cites":["7e2bf42c-6255-4fd7-9d74-7866cde485f3"]},{"text":"The dozens of bastard children scattered through the kingdom stirred real resentment, enough to nearly tip France back into civil strife.","source_id":"af6c2d1f-72f5-4778-94a1-466874d65049","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":1},{"text":"Worse, he meant to marry his favourite, Gabrielle d'Estrées — an outrage to the raison d'état — and only her premature death stopped the infamy.","source_id":"af6c2d1f-72f5-4778-94a1-466874d65049","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":1},{"text":"As Femme Ladoucette wrote to the Queen, in the kingdom of France one separated the sheep from the goats.","source_id":"af6c2d1f-72f5-4778-94a1-466874d65049","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":1},{"text":"As king, from 1589 to 1610, he vowed to make Paris a wonder of the world, and he delivered — the elegant Pont Neuf, whose \"new bridge\" name hides the fact that it's the oldest in Paris, the Place Dauphine across the water, and the Place Royale, later renamed the Place des Vosges.","source_id":"7e2bf42c-6255-4fd7-9d74-7866cde485f3","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":1},{"text":"Born and raised a Protestant, he converted to Catholicism, the faith of the majority, to end the religious wars that by the close of the sixteenth century had left Paris starving and looking like a bomb site, and then, detesting partisanship, he signed the Edict of Nantes in 1598, writing tolerance for the very religion he'd renounced into law.","source_id":"7e2bf42c-6255-4fd7-9d74-7866cde485f3","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":1},{"text":"The fanatical Catholic who stabbed him to death, Francis Ravaillac, was not persuaded.","source_id":"7e2bf42c-6255-4fd7-9d74-7866cde485f3","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":1},{"text":"And yet Henri IV is still one of France's heroes, named beside Charlemagne, Joan of Arc, and Saint-Louis IX — the king who declared kindness and mercy the first virtues of a prince.","source_id":"7e2bf42c-6255-4fd7-9d74-7866cde485f3","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":1},{"text":"He'd have approved of what became of this spot — a tranquil, tree-lined garden, still a favourite haunt of lovers.","source_id":"53261606-2bd8-4862-829f-6730c31f2b4d","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":1},{"text":"The prime place to stand is the little knoll of trees at the extreme point of the island, and from here you can even hop one of the river boats docking on the north side.","source_id":"53261606-2bd8-4862-829f-6730c31f2b4d","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":1},{"text":"Look out and you'll see why people linger — the Hôtel de la Monnaie and the dome of the Institut de France on your left, the Louvre on your right, the Pont-des-Arts straight ahead, and by night the whole square turns to enchantment.","source_id":"391c501b-9c3d-49e0-91fb-ebe55a456262","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":1}]}
